school.en: Beijing National Day School Tianjin Experimental School

lead.en: A campus that keeps growing — step inside. 19+ open communities, a whole day of light, work in the corridors and a few furry residents. Pick a place, put your headphones on, and let us tell you about it.

text.en: We filmed a day on campus — morning light, works along the corridors, arguments in class, and the people who never want to leave after school. Watch first, then step into each community.

chooseSub.en: 19 communities, numbered in tour order. Open any of them for photos, a short text, and audio guides in Chinese and English.

en.name: Main Hall
paras: Welcome to the main hall — the most open and lively space on campus. We gather here in the morning, catch the sun at noon, and still hang around after school.
The walls change all the time: today a student exhibition, tomorrow the results of a project. It works like a mirror of what is happening in this school every day.

en.name: Campus Shop
paras: The campus shop is more than a place to buy things. Many notebooks, badges and tote bags start as student designs — sketch, sample, shelf, all in one project.
Ten-minute breaks are the busiest. Students also take turns at the till, restocking and bookkeeping.

en.name: Star Brew Café
paras: Star Brew is a café founded and run by students. The menu, the pricing, the shifts and the cost sheets are all decided by the student team; teachers just watch.
It is also where teachers and students talk most easily — a lot of ideas start over one cup of milk tea.

en.name: STEM Community
paras: The STEM community has six workshops: wood, metal, electronics, robotics, flight simulation and digital fabrication. The corridor shows work by Grade 2 and 3 — walking cars, water rockets that actually fly.
Here the question is never “what is the answer”, but “how do you want it to move”.

en.name: Meow House
paras: Meow House took in four cats that wandered here while the campus was being built, and later three chinchillas adopted from our sister school in Beijing. They are now the most popular residents.
Feeding, cleaning and health records are on a student rota. Caring for another life is a very concrete lesson in responsibility.

en.name: Art Community
paras: The art community is the most colourful and the most relaxing place on campus. Ceramics, printmaking, mixed media and digital painting share one open floor.
The corridor is the gallery. Work is not judged on how realistic it looks, but on what you want to say and why.

en.name: Music Community
paras: Music and drama lessons both happen here. The middle of the hall is the rehearsal area; practice rooms and a small recording booth sit on either side, and drumbeats leak through the doors.
For the end-of-term show, students handle everything: repertoire, rehearsals, posters and lighting.

en.name: Weilan Theatre
paras: Weilan is our own theatre: a proscenium stage, retractable seating, a full lighting and sound system. Plays, musicals and grade shows all happen here.
Rigging, lighting programming and front-of-house are run by a student technical crew. They are already busy two weeks before the curtain goes up.

en.name: Cinema
paras: The cinema sits next to the theatre and opens twice a week. The seats recline, the screen is not huge, but the sound is good.
The film club votes on the programme: classics, documentaries, and short films shot by students. Screenings usually end with a discussion nobody wants to leave.

en.name: Green Box
paras: The Green Box is a glass room wrapped in plants, with beautiful light. Small exhibitions, reading clubs, parent salons and project launches all happen here.
It is only one storey high, yet almost the quietest place in school — sit down and you can hear the leaves move.

en.name: Dance Studio
paras: The dance studio has a full wall of mirrors, a long barre and a sprung floor that gives a little under bare feet.
Chinese dance, contemporary and street dance clubs share it in turns. The rehearsal timetable taped to the mirror is completely full.

en.name: Black Box
paras: The Black Box is a studio theatre painted black on all sides: no fixed stage, movable seating, light from any direction.
Experimental theatre, improvisation and script readings happen here. The smaller the space, the closer the performance — audiences often sit right beside the actors.

en.name: Animation Studio
paras: The animation studio is half drawing room, half computer lab: light boxes and animation paper on one side, pen displays on the other.
Club projects start with character design and end with a two- or three-minute short each term — storyboard, colouring, voice recording and editing, the whole pipeline.

en.name: Dining Hall
paras: The dining hall is the most punctual place in school: breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack, three times a day, never late. The kitchen is open to view.
Next door, the food workshop runs cooking classes — washing, chopping, plating, all by students. The menu listens to student feedback too.

en.name: Sports Hall
paras: The sports hall is an indoor multi-court arena: two basketball courts convert into volleyball or badminton, with movable seating around them.
PE on rainy days, club leagues and whole-school assemblies all happen here. The wooden floor is mopped every afternoon.

en.name: Outdoor Terrace
paras: The terrace sits on the second floor with a timber deck and low planting beds along the edge. On fine days you can bring lunch up here.
It looks over the sports field and the courtyards, and it is the best place on campus for sunset.

en.name: Sports Field
paras: The field is a standard oval inside a blue track: a football pitch in the middle, a ring of lanes around it, bleachers and a long-jump pit at the edge.
During the ten-minute break the lanes are full of runners; on sports day the bleachers are full of noise.

en.name: Grade 8 Community
paras: Grade 8 is a flexible learning community: no fixed classrooms, an open learning area in the middle, seminar rooms and quiet pods around it.
The timetable is posted at the entrance and students find their own spot. During project week the space fills with drawings, models and arguments.

en.name: Grade 4 Community
paras: The Grade 4 community is hosting an exhibition: “When Ten Meets a Thousand — China's World Heritage”. Every booth was chosen, researched and scripted by students.
Ten-year-olds telling thousand-year stories — seriously, and in their own way.
